detail:
MEASURED, not theorised. Repro: migrate a legacy store to v3 (no membership exists, so admission default-allows `write`), then admit a normal post-upgrade policy — a `membership` granting one human rule+write in `src/catalog/`. Then call store.rebuild(). Result: acknowledged_events_lost = 1, id reported, journal row `rejected: unauthorized`. The lost event was a derived `amended` event authored by the migrator principal, which the new membership does not name.

Why only ONE of ~16 migrator-authored events: admit() takes ONE view snapshot per pass and loops up to 32 passes. Events settled in pass 1 (before the membership was admitted) saw no policy and were default-allowed; only events that were still pending_parents when the membership landed were judged against it. So WHICH previously-admitted events survive a rebuild depends on how many admission passes they happened to need. That is worse than a uniform denial: it is not reproducible from the event set alone.

This contradicts C14/C16 A3.7 ("destroying and rebuilding the materialized view loses no acknowledged event") and ADR §4.2 ("no acknowledged event is ever silently lost"). It is not fully silent — rebuild() returns acknowledged_events_lost and the ids — but the events do leave the projection.

FIX TRIED AND REJECTED inside lane 02c: seed a membership at migration time naming the migrator as a causal ancestor of every migration event. It does fix the rebuild (lost 0), but any seeded membership can only be replaced by a principal it grants `rule`, so the store's policy is locked to the migrator forever — and the next thing that broke in the probe was exactly that: the operator's own post-upgrade membership was rejected as unauthorized. Trading a rebuild hazard for a permanent policy lockout is the worse bargain, so the migration seeds NO policy and the note is in the code.

PROPOSED FIX (lane 02b / the lead, admission seam): make the admission decision durable, or evaluate capability against the policy in force at the event's causal position rather than against admittedView().membership (which is `memberships.at(-1)`). Either removes the retroactive re-judgement; the second also makes admission a pure function of the causal history, which is what determinism requires.

WORKAROUND for anyone hitting this now: a replacement membership must carry forward a `write` grant for every principal already present in the history, including the migrator principal in .twining/store.json's companion id-map.
summary: rebuild() re-evaluates capability against the LATEST membership, so a policy added after migration drops already-admitted events — ordering-dependently
